summary: Fewer than half of laid-off workers get written notice ahead of time.
realLife: The survey found about 45 percent had written advance notice; plant closings had the most (about 58 percent), then abolished positions (about 42) and too little work (about 32).
sources: Bureau of Labor Statistics, Worker Displacement news release (Jan 2023 to Dec 2025): https://www.bls.gov/news.release/disp.nr0.htm
inGame: Job-ended event could carry a notice flag by reason; no notice or WARN records exist, so it needs: advance-notice field on the job-ended event. Scene: needs a producer for layoff-terms.

turns.summary: The employer gives written notice weeks before the job ends, so the person has time to plan.
pulledBy: a layoff event announced in advance
turns.writesBack: A note in the journal, the person's mood steadier, and an earlier start on the job search.

turns.summary: The person hears about the cut the same day it takes effect, with nothing in writing.
pulledBy: a small employer short of money
turns.writesBack: Trust in the employer drops, the mood turns sour, and coworkers talk about it.

turns.summary: Coworkers hear rumors for days before the written notice finally arrives.
turns.writesBack: Worry spreads, ties among coworkers tighten, and a journal note records the wait.
